People look at dividends differently then I do. Higher dividend actually worries me cause its a sign the company is struggling and if it keeps going higher that dividend is at high risk of getting cut or suspended. Even if they just freeze the dividend from being raised the following year can hurt the stock. Market knows this and they start to short the stock or they stay away and then the sentiment starts to get more negative.

Yes it can be a value trap if dividend gets too high.  They aren't using cash they earned so comes from a cash reserve or selling assets or debt or dilution of stock. You have to read the financials to find it to know for sure.

Or you can stop focusing on the dividend when it doesn’t give you extra money than you already had in principal anyway. Dividend pays out your share price drops by the payout amount. People that over analyze dividends especially when they just DRIP don't understand the math to begin with. You can pay yourself a "dividend" any time as it's no different than just selling your principal down hy whatever you want your "dividend" to be.

I understand what you're saying and I have growth stocks. A covered dividend gives you more diversity of a portfolio for when growth stocks go down. A covered dividend is cash given to you by the management and you dont have to sell shares of stocks at a bad time to get income. Also you can drip the dividends back into the stock it came out of or into different positions. Then during recessions dividend stocks normally go down less than nondividend stocks. Then Metta made so much fcf it didn't have enough good stuff to invest the money in and found out its more profitable to pay out dividends. Companies have a handful of things it can do with its free cash. Pay you, pay off debt, buy back shares, invest in other assets, capex, or invest in other companies. Its good have growth stocks, cash covered high yield dividend stocks, and stocks pay a lower dividend that grow the dividend.  And just because a dividend is paid doesnt mean price of stock goes down by its dividend.
